Ana y Pablo están en la estación. Un tren llega. Ana tiene su boleto en la mano. Pablo tiene su boleto en una bolsa.

—¿Tienes tu boleto? —pregunta Ana.

—Sí, tengo mi boleto —dice Pablo.

Pablo abre la bolsa. Pablo saca el boleto.

—Mi boleto es para Madrid —dice Ana—. ¿Tu boleto también es para Madrid?

Pablo mira su boleto.

—No. Mi boleto es para Toledo.

Ana mira el boleto de Pablo. En el boleto dice: «Destino: Toledo». En el boleto de Ana dice: «Destino: Madrid».

—¡Tenemos boletos para destinos diferentes! —dice Ana—. Yo tengo un boleto para Madrid y tú tienes un boleto para Toledo.

—Pero yo quiero ir a Madrid contigo —dice Pablo.

Ana mira el reloj. Después, Ana señala una ventanilla. Una mujer está detrás de la ventanilla.

—Vamos a preguntar —dice Ana.

Pablo toma su bolsa. Los dos amigos caminan hacia la ventanilla con sus boletos.

glossary.meaning: And; joins people or ideas.
To be in a place; están is used for two people, está for one.
In or at; indicates location.
The; used with a feminine singular noun.
Railway station.
A; used with a masculine singular noun.
Train.
To arrive; llega means the train arrives.
To have; tengo means I have, tienes means you have, tiene means he or she has, and tenemos means we have.
His or her; identifies something belonging to Ana or Pablo.
Ticket for a train journey; boletos is plural.
Hand; Ana holds her ticket in her hand.
A; used with a feminine singular noun.
Bag.
Your; used before a noun when speaking to one person. Unlike tú, it has no accent.
To ask a question; pregunta means asks.
Yes; an affirmative answer.
My; identifies the speaker's ticket.
To say; dice introduces speech or tells what is written on a ticket.
To open; abre means Pablo opens the bag.
To take out; saca means Pablo takes the ticket out of his bag.
The; used with a masculine singular noun.
To be; es identifies the destination the ticket is for.
For; introduces the destination a ticket is for.
Also or too; asks whether the other ticket is for the same destination.
To look at; mira describes looking at a ticket or the clock.
No; a negative answer.
Of or belonging to; links a ticket to its owner.
Destination: the place a journey goes to; destinos is plural.
Different; diferentes describes destinations that are not the same.
I; explicitly names the speaker as the subject.
You; the subject pronoun for one person addressed informally.
But; introduces a contrast with the ticket's destination.
To want; quiero means I want.
To go to; followed here by the desired destination.
With you; Pablo wants to travel with Ana.
Clock; Ana looks at it to check the time.
Then or afterward; introduces the next action.
To point to; señala means Ana points to the ticket window.
Ticket or service window at the station.
Woman.
Behind; describes the woman's position relative to the window.
Let's go and ask; suggests asking at the ticket window.
To pick up or take; toma means Pablo takes his bag.
Both or the two; refers to Ana and Pablo together.
Friend; amigos is plural and refers to the two friends.
To walk; caminan means the two friends walk.
Toward; indicates the direction they walk.
With; they bring their tickets with them.
Their; used before the plural noun for the friends' tickets.
